chapter: Stuff Smith, CBS and radio work
title: Chronology of Stuff Smith, Ellis Larkins and CBS
summary: Hall works through the order of Stuff Smith's Chicago job and the Larkins trio, using his daughter's birth.

story.theme_name: Chicago: the jazz migration and its clubs
story.community_name: Going north: working the Chicago jazz scene

blocks.x: Now, in between the time you and Bill left the Teddy Wilson sextet and the time that you and Bill joined up with Ellis, what were you doing?
Catching hell. (Laughter)
You weren't doing too much? How long a period was that?
Well, then I got with, then I did get with CBS, I worked with CBS as a staff person.
Well, where does Stuff Smith come in?
Stuff Smith was in '41.
Right after Teddy Wilson's big band and before Teddy Wilson's sextet would you say?
It was before the Teddy Wilson sextet.
Okay, but before Ellis Larkin?
Larkin
Yeah.
So it was the period when you were scuffling but you didn't go --
No, I'd been working with Ellis Larkin.
Oh, and Bill Coleman?
Yeah.
In the --
In the Cafe Society Uptown.
And then you went with Stuff Smith?
Then I went with Stuff Smith.

What year was that, you say '41, but according to this, you played with Ellis Larkin in '42 or '43, that's what I was trying to determine. You said you went to Chicago with Stuff to play the Garrett Show Bar.
Yeah.
Was it with the trio?
No, with Herman Autrey (inaudible) and Sammy Benskin? and a tenor player --
Cap McCord, Bob McCord? There was a Cap McCord that played with Louis Armstrong, some record in Paris in 19 --
Cass McCord?
Cass -- maybe.
There was a Cass McCord and Slick Jones, who had been the former drummer with Fats.
Right, so you think that was '41?
That was '41, '42 because Barbara was born then, she was born when I was out there.
I see. So then, Ellis Larkin, Bill and yourself was before Stuff Smith? At the Cafe Society Uptown?
Let me get back to that.
All right.
Let me think about that.
Okay.
Because I was working with Ellis Larkin again at the Blue Angel when I got into the theater bit.
Ah, okay, Ellis Larkin at Blue Angel '42 and '43, so this was another time around with Ellis Larkin?
Yeah.
Okay, so the first time was Bill Coleman and yourself with Ellis in '41; then you went with Stuff and that's when you read this article, you said?
Yeah, when I was with Stuff in Chicago.
In Chicago.
In Chicago, yeah.
